name: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
description: Infrared space telescope focused on exoplanet atmospheres, galaxy formation, and deep universe observations.
epwRelevance: Very High — atmospheric characterization of transiting exoplanets

name: Hubble Space Telescope (HST)
description: Optical and ultraviolet space telescope providing long-term observations of stars, galaxies, and exoplanet atmospheres.
epwRelevance: High — legacy and ongoing transit spectroscopy

name: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS)
description: All-sky survey mission discovering transiting exoplanets around bright nearby stars.
epwRelevance: Very High — primary source of EPW targets

name: Characterizing Exoplanet Satellite (CHEOPS)
description: High-precision photometry mission focused on known exoplanets.
epwRelevance: High — precise transit follow-up and planet radius refinement

name: Pandora
description: Small space telescope studying exoplanet atmospheres while separating planetary signals from stellar variability.
epwRelevance: Very High — directly connected to transit timing, stellar variability, and follow-up observations

name: Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx)
description: All-sky near-infrared spectral survey mission mapping hundreds of millions of galaxies and stars.
epwRelevance: Medium — useful stellar and infrared survey context for exoplanet host environments

name: Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network (LCO)
description: A worldwide network of robotic telescopes used for time-domain astronomy and exoplanet follow-up.
epwRelevance: Very High — ground-based transit follow-up similar to EPW observing goals

name: Search For Habitable Planets Eclipsing Ultra-Cool Stars (SPECULOOS)
description: Ground-based telescope network searching for transiting planets around ultra-cool dwarf stars.
epwRelevance: High — discovers and follows small transiting planets around nearby cool stars

name: Transiting Planets and Planetesimals Small Telescope (TRAPPIST)
description: Small robotic telescopes known for exoplanet transit discoveries and follow-up of small planets.
epwRelevance: High — iconic ground-based transit discovery and follow-up system

name: Next Generation Transit Survey (NGTS)
description: Array of robotic telescopes designed to detect transiting exoplanets around bright stars.
epwRelevance: High — ground-based transit discovery and follow-up pipeline

name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (RST)
description: Wide-field infrared telescope for microlensing, dark energy studies, and direct imaging technology demonstrations.
epwRelevance: High — future exoplanet microlensing discoveries and direct imaging demonstrations

name: Planetary Transits and Oscillations (PLATO)
description: Mission designed to find and characterize Earth-like exoplanets around bright stars.
epwRelevance: Very High — future source of long-period transiting exoplanets

name: Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large-survey (ARIEL)
description: Dedicated space telescope mission to study the atmospheres of a large sample of exoplanets.
epwRelevance: Very High — atmospheric survey mission for known transiting exoplanets

name: Extremely Large Telescope (ELT)
description: Future 39-meter class ground-based telescope designed for high-resolution astronomy, including exoplanet imaging and atmospheric studies.

name: Gaia
description: Precision astrometry mission that mapped positions, distances, and motions of stars across the Milky Way.
epwRelevance: High — stellar parameters, companion checks, distances, and transit validation

name: Kepler Space Telescope
description: Revolutionized exoplanet discovery with thousands of detected and confirmed planet candidates.
epwRelevance: Very High — foundational exoplanet catalog and transit discovery mission

name: Spitzer Space Telescope
description: Infrared space telescope used for exoplanet atmosphere studies and precision transit observations.
epwRelevance: High — legacy infrared transit and atmospheric observations

name: Convection, Rotation and Planetary Transits (CoRoT)
description: Early space mission designed for stellar seismology and transiting exoplanet discovery.
epwRelevance: Medium — important early space-based transit discovery mission
